title: Diomedes and Glaucus Exchange Armor
text:
In the middle of a battle before Troy, the Greek hero Diomedes found himself facing Glaucus, a leader of the Lycians fighting for the Trojans. Before attacking, Diomedes asked who he was, in case he might be a god.

Glaucus answered with a famous reflection: the generations of men are like leaves, scattered on the ground by the wind and growing again in spring. Then he told his family history. His grandfather was the hero Bellerophon, who had come to Lycia, killed the Chimera, and married a king's daughter.

When Diomedes heard the name, he was delighted. He drove his spear into the earth. His own grandfather Oeneus, he said, had once welcomed Bellerophon as a guest for twenty days, and the two had exchanged gifts of friendship. That made Glaucus and Diomedes guest friends by inheritance. There were plenty of other enemies to fight, he said, so they should avoid each other in battle, and exchange armor so that everyone could see their bond.

They leapt from their chariots, clasped hands and pledged friendship. Then they swapped armor. Homer notes wryly that Zeus must have taken away Glaucus's wits, for he gave gold armor worth a hundred oxen for bronze worth nine.
lesson: Old bonds of friendship and hospitality deserve to be honored even when circumstances put you on opposite sides. Look for what connects you before you fight.
